title: Fund Selection Policy
description: How we select funds for recommendations.

intro.heading: Fund & Product Selection Policy
intro.subtitle: Per AMFI DDQ Section 2.6 | AMFI Master Circular | SEBI Guidelines on Suitability & Conflict of Interest
intro.summaryLine: Innovate Securities Pvt. Ltd. | ARN-42505 | Valid: 06-Apr-2024 to 05-Apr-2027 | Effective: August 2026
intro.notice: This Fund & Product Selection Policy describes the framework used by Innovate Securities to select, recommend, and review financial products for investors. This policy is prepared in accordance with AMFI DDQ Section 2.6, AMFI Master Circular January 2026, and applicable SEBI guidelines on investor suitability and conflict of interest management. We are committed to recommending only those products that are genuinely suitable for each investor based on their individual profile.

blocks.heading: Core Principle — Suitability Above All
blocks.body: Every product recommendation is based SOLELY on the investor’s risk profile, financial goals, investment horizon, and financial capacity. Commission rates, incentives, or commercial considerations from AMCs have NO influence on our recommendations. Investor suitability is non-negotiable.

items.title: Investor Profiling
items.body: Structured risk assessment covering goals, horizon, income, liabilities, and risk tolerance

items.title: Product Mapping
items.body: Match investor profile to suitable product categories using SEBI Riskometer and asset allocation

items.title: Scheme Evaluation
items.body: Evaluate schemes using quantitative and qualitative criteria — performance, costs, AMC reputation

items.title: Recommendation & Review
items.body: Present suitable options. Final decision always with the investor. Periodic review at least annually.

blocks.heading: 2. Investor Risk Profiling
blocks.intro: Before recommending any product, Innovate Securities conducts a structured investor risk profiling exercise covering:
bullets: Age & Life Stage — Investment horizon typically decreases as investors approach retirement
Income & Surplus — Monthly investable surplus after expenses and emergency fund allocation
Existing Liabilities — Home loan, personal loan, education loan EMIs affecting investable capacity
Financial Goals — Short-term (less than 3 years), medium-term (3–7 years), long-term (7+ years)
Risk Tolerance — Emotional and financial capacity to absorb temporary portfolio losses
Investment Experience — First-time investor vs experienced investor — affects product complexity
Tax Bracket — Relevant for recommending tax-efficient investment options like ELSS
Liquidity Needs — Emergency fund adequacy, upcoming financial commitments in next 3 years

blocks.heading: 3. Risk Profile Categories & Product Suitability Matrix
rows: Conservative — Low risk tolerance, capital preservation priority
Liquid, Overnight, Ultra Short Duration, Money Market, Short Duration Debt, Conservative Hybrid
Small Cap, Sector/Thematic, Long Duration Debt, High Yield Credit
Balanced Advantage, Aggressive Hybrid, Large Cap, Multi Cap, Index Funds, Balanced Hybrid
Hybrid MFs, Large Cap MFs, Index Funds
Small Cap (primary), Sector Funds (primary), Long Duration Debt
Aggressive — High risk tolerance, wealth creation focus
Flexi Cap, Mid Cap, Small Cap, ELSS, Thematic, Sectoral, International Funds
Liquid/Overnight for long-term goals, Capital Protection schemes

blocks.body: This matrix is indicative. Actual recommendations depend on the individual investor’s complete profile. A Moderate investor may hold some Aggressive products for long-term goals and vice versa, based on goal-based allocation.

items.title: Performance Track Record
items.body: 3-year and 5-year returns vs benchmark and category average. Consistency of outperformance across market cycles.

items.title: Fund Manager Quality
items.body: Fund manager’s experience, track record across market cycles, stability (low turnover), and investment philosophy.

items.title: AMC Reputation & Stability
items.body: AMC’s AUM size, years of operation, parent company stability, regulatory compliance history, and overall franchise strength.

items.title: Expense Ratio (TER)
items.body: Total Expense Ratio compared to category average. Lower TER (all else equal) means better net returns for investors.

items.title: Risk-Adjusted Returns
items.body: Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, Standard Deviation — evaluating how much return is generated per unit of risk taken.

items.title: Liquidity & Portfolio Quality
items.body: Portfolio concentration, liquidity of underlying securities, credit quality (for debt), sector/stock concentration risks.

items.title: Fund Size (AUM)
items.body: Adequate AUM to ensure liquidity and operational efficiency. Avoid very small funds with closure risk and very large funds in mid/small cap categories.

items.title: Investment Style Consistency
items.body: Does the fund follow its stated investment mandate? Style drift (e.g. large cap fund buying small caps) is a red flag.

blocks.heading: 5. Conflict of Interest Policy — Formal Declaration
blocks.body: Innovate Securities formally declares that: Commission rates received from AMCs have NO influence on fund recommendations | We do not maintain any formal or informal “preferred AMC” list for commercial reasons | We do not participate in AMC-sponsored holidays, trips, or gifts that create conflict of interest | We do not receive any incentives, rebates, or benefits beyond the standard trail commission disclosed on our website | Scheme recommendations are documented with rationale before presentation to investors | We do not switch investors between schemes to generate additional commission (churning) | Direct Plans are always disclosed as an alternative, even though we do not facilitate them

blocks.heading: Practices We Strictly Prohibit (Conflict of Interest)
bullets: Recommending schemes based on higher commission rates or incentives
Churning — unnecessary switching of investor portfolios to generate commissions
Accepting non-cash benefits, gifts above regulatory limits, or sponsored trips from AMCs
Recommending close-ended NFOs or illiquid products without full risk disclosure
Recommending products outside investor risk profile without written unsuitability declaration

items.title: Inform
items.body: Clearly communicate in writing that the chosen product is outside the investor’s risk profile

items.title: Explain Risks
items.body: Detail volatility, liquidity, and downside potential of the product

items.title: Formal Declaration
items.body: Investor signs a formal Unsuitability Declaration acknowledging the risk mismatch

items.title: Process Transaction
items.body: Transaction processed only after receiving the signed declaration

items.title: Record Keeping
items.body: Unsuitability declarations retained for a minimum of 8 years

blocks.heading: 7. Portfolio Review Policy
bullets: Annual Review: comprehensive portfolio review with every investor at least once a year
Triggered Review: additional reviews when there is a material change in investor’s financial situation, goals, or life stage
Market Event Review: during significant market events (15%+ correction or rally), investors are proactively communicated with
Fund Change Review: when a recommended scheme undergoes fundamental changes (fund manager change, mandate change, merger), investors are informed and alternatives reviewed
Rebalancing: recommended when actual asset allocation deviates significantly (more than 10%) from target allocation

blocks.heading: 8. Record Keeping & Compliance
bullets: All investor risk profiles, financial goal discussions, and recommendation rationale are documented and maintained
Records retained for minimum 8 years as per SEBI and AMFI requirements
All unsuitability declarations maintained as permanent client records
This Fund Selection Policy is reviewed and updated at least annually or when there are regulatory changes
Policy is available for inspection by AMFI, SEBI, or any regulatory authority on request

blocks.body: Formal Declaration by Innovate Securities: This Fund & Product Selection Policy represents our genuine commitment to investor-first recommendations and is followed in letter and spirit in all client interactions.
